title: Star trails hanging over La Silla
caption: Star trails over La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Star trails hang in the sky above ESO's La Silla Observatory. This photograph by Alexandre Santerne was captured with a long series of exposures taken at night.

The trails come from the apparent motion of the sky. The stars are not moving in the way they seem to be; Earth is turning on its axis, and the observatory and camera turn with it. From the ground, that rotation makes every star appear to travel slowly across the sky.

Each frame freezes the stars in one position. When the frames are combined, those positions join into curved lines, showing in a single image a motion too slow to follow by eye. The technique turns an ordinary starry night into a picture of our planet's spin, with the observatory standing still beneath it.

understand.summary: This is a series of night-time photographs taken in visible light with a camera at La Silla and combined into one image. The exposure settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as points; the trails appear only because many exposures were combined.

explore: La Silla is one of ESO's observatory sites in Chile, and its telescopes and dark skies are a frequent subject for ESO's Photo Ambassadors. Alexandre Santerne is one of them.
